guard_streams.source: Latest telecoms and pay-TV complaints revealed - Q1 2025
guard_streams.write_limit: Quarterly complaint rankings are service-quality context and cannot establish selected-parcel broadband coverage, live orderability or measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Q1 2025 complaints update on 7 August 2025.
The figures cover January to March 2025.
Overall complaints remained similar to the previous quarter.
Fixed-broadband complaints increased.
Pay-TV complaints increased.
Landline and pay-monthly mobile complaint levels stayed the same.
TalkTalk was the most complained-about broadband provider.
Plusnet generated the fewest broadband complaints.
EE and TalkTalk were the most complained-about landline providers.
Utility Warehouse generated the fewest landline complaints.

guard_streams.source: Latest telecoms and pay-TV complaints revealed - Q2 2025
guard_streams.write_limit: Quarterly complaint volumes and provider rankings are aggregate service-quality indicators, not parcel availability or performance evidence.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Q2 2025 complaints update on 30 October 2025.
The figures cover April to June 2025.
Overall complaint numbers decreased from the previous quarter.
Fixed-broadband, landline and pay-TV complaints decreased.
Pay-monthly mobile complaints stayed the same.
EE was the most complained-about provider across broadband, landline and pay-TV.
It was the first time since late 2023 that one provider was worst across three services.
Plusnet was the least complained-about fixed-broadband provider.
Utility Warehouse had the fewest landline complaints for a sixth consecutive quarter.
Faults, service quality and getting connected remained the main broadband and landline complaint reasons.

guard_streams.source: Report: Complaints about broadband, landline, mobile and pay-TV services
guard_streams.write_limit: The complaints series normalises provider complaints for comparison and cannot verify physical serviceability or measured speed at a selected parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the complaints report page on 25 January 2024.
The report page was updated on 23 July 2026.
The series covers landline, fixed broadband, pay-monthly mobile and pay-TV services.
Provider complaint rates are calculated relative to customer bases per 100,000 subscribers.
Ofcom publishes the provider comparison quarterly.
In Q1 2026 overall complaints decreased from Q4 2025.
Q1 2026 fixed-broadband and pay-monthly mobile complaints decreased.
Q1 2026 landline and pay-TV complaints stayed the same.
The report provides interactive charts that can be filtered by provider and year.
A background and methodology document supports interpretation and provider comparability.

guard_streams.write_limit: An evaluation plan and programme-management snapshot do not establish current serviceability, orderability or measured speed for a selected parcel.

facts.detail: The Project Gigabit Evaluation Plan was published on 15 August 2025.
Ipsos UK authored the plan as BDUK's commissioned evaluator.
The plan covers Project Gigabit, GIS interventions and the Gigabit Broadband Voucher Scheme.
The plan describes gigabit-capable networks as offering download speeds of at least 1,000 Mbps.
GBVS vouchers are described as worth up to £4,500.
The GigaHubs element is not covered by this evaluation plan.
As of autumn 2024, procurement activity had been completed in 36 local areas.
The plan expected approximately 50 GIS contracts to be issued.
Contracts issued at the snapshot covered about 586,100 premises at a cost of £942 million.
GIS civil-engineering delivery was expected to run from 2024 to at least 2030.

guard_streams.source: Local Full Fibre Network programme evaluation plan
guard_streams.write_limit: A programme evaluation framework concerns historic intervention design and outcomes, not current selected-parcel broadband availability or speed.

facts.detail: The LFFN programme evaluation plan was published on 15 August 2025.
LFFN was a £200 million programme.
The programme was launched in 2017.
The plan records that only 2% of UK premises had full-fibre access in 2016.
The current evaluation covers waves two and three.
The evaluation is structured around six work packages.
One work package examines broadband-market competition and supplier expansion.
The evaluation includes consumer outcomes such as affordability and choice.
Work package two scheduled data collection from May to November 2025.
Work package two scheduled a final report for April 2026 and publication for June 2026.
